thread.title: Stock Market Gets a Head Start on Summer

title: Stock Market Gets a Head Start on Summer
text:
Stock Market Gets a Head Start on Summer By aapl
Despite a sharp drop in oil, a bounce in bonds and comments that the Korean summit would likely be held at some point after all, it was a lackluster day of action for the stock market. An early bounce was sold and the indices closed with minor losses. Breadth was negative and the early momentum in some big-cap names such as Alibaba ( BABA ) and Apple ( AAPL ) faded.
For the week, the indices ended up with slight gains. It was see-saw action and the only real drama came on the announcement about the North Korean meeting. There continues to be some reaction to the trade issues with China, but that controversy didn't produce any sustained movement.
What we have is trading range action. Indices held steady and failed to generate any momentum in either direction. There was some news flow to react to but nothing that generated any real emotion.
The bulls will argue that this action is healthy consolidation that is building a foundation for an upside thrust. The bears will contend that this is stalling action and the lack of conviction among buyers is a sign that the indices will encounter problems.
The opportunistic trader will point out that there has been some decent trading in individual stocks even though the indices have been flat. That may change next week but we'll worry about that after the long weekend.
Enjoy the holiday. Summer is here. I'll see you on Tuesday. Get an email alert each time I write an article for Real Money. Click the "+Follow" next to my byline to this article. More From James "Rev Shark" DePorre
